subject: religion
title: The Life of Prophet Muhammad (SM)
summary: The early life, prophethood, Meccan and Medinan periods, and key teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (SM)

sections.title: Early Life and Background
sections.content: Prophet Muhammad (SM) was born in 570 CE in Makkah, in the tribe of Quraysh. His father Abdullah died before his birth, and his mother Amina died when he was six. He was raised by his grandfather Abdul Muttalib and later by his uncle Abu Talib. As a young man, he earned the title Al-Amin (the trustworthy) for his honesty and integrity. He worked as a shepherd and later as a merchant. At age 25, he married Khadijah (RA), a wealthy businesswoman.

sections.title: The Beginning of Prophethood
sections.content: At age 40, while meditating in the Cave of Hira, Prophet Muhammad (SM) received the first revelation through the angel Jibril (Gabriel). The first revealed words were 'Iqra' (Read) from Surah Al-Alaq. For the next 23 years, the Quran was revealed progressively. He first preached secretly to his family and close friends. Khadijah, Ali, Abu Bakr, and Zayd were among the first believers. After three years, he began preaching publicly, calling people to worship one God and abandon idolatry.

sections.title: The Meccan and Medinan Periods
sections.content: The Meccan period (13 years) was marked by persecution of Muslims. Despite torture, boycott, and social ostracism, the Prophet remained patient. In 622 CE, facing increasing hostility, he migrated to Madinah (the Hijrah), which marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar. In Madinah, he established the first Islamic state, united the Ansar and Muhajirun, and drafted the Constitution of Madinah. Major battles including Badr, Uhud, and Khandaq occurred during this period.

sections.title: Key Teachings and Legacy
sections.content: The Prophet's teachings emphasized monotheism (Tawhid), justice, charity, honesty, and compassion. His farewell sermon during his final Hajj laid out core Islamic principles: equality of all humans, rights of women, prohibition of usury and injustice. He taught that the best among people are those who are most beneficial to others. His Sunnah (traditions) and Hadith (sayings) guide Muslims in all aspects of life. He passed away in 632 CE at age 63 in Madinah.
